title: Wish / If Only
subtitle: Express regret and unreal wishes about the present and the past.
objectives: Use wish/if only + past simple for a present wish
Use wish/if only + past perfect for a past regret
Use wish/if only + would for a complaint about someone else's behavior

content.intro: "Wish" and "if only" (a stronger, more emotional version of wish) let you express that reality is different from what you want — in the present, or looking back at the past.

rules.heading: a) Present wish — wish/if only + past simple
rules.body:
• I wish I had more free time. (I don't have much now)
  • If only I spoke French. (I don't speak French)

rules.heading: b) Past regret — wish/if only + past perfect
rules.body:
• I wish I had studied harder. (I didn't, and now I regret it)
  • If only I hadn't said that. (I did say it, and I regret it)

rules.heading: c) Complaint about someone's behavior — wish + would
rules.body:
• I wish you would stop interrupting me. (a complaint/request for change, annoyance)

Not used for yourself: "I wish I would..." isn't standard — use "I wish I could" or "I wish I did/had."

examples: I wish I had more free time.
I wish I had studied harder.
If only I hadn't said that.
I wish you would stop interrupting me.
She wishes she could travel more.

commonMistakes.wrong: I wish I have more time.
commonMistakes.right: I wish I had more time.
commonMistakes.why: A present wish needs the past simple form (had), not the present.

commonMistakes.wrong: I wish I studied harder. (regretting a past choice)
commonMistakes.right: I wish I had studied harder.
commonMistakes.why: A past regret needs the past perfect (had studied), not the simple past.

commonMistakes.wrong: I wish I would speak French.
commonMistakes.right: I wish I spoke French. / I wish I could speak French.
commonMistakes.why: "Wish + would" isn't used for your own ability/state — use the past simple or "could" instead.

commonMistakes.wrong: I wish you stop interrupting me.
commonMistakes.right: I wish you would stop interrupting me.
commonMistakes.why: A complaint about someone else's behavior needs "wish + would."

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form.

items.prompt: I wish I ___ (have) more free time. (present wish)
I wish I ___ (study) harder for the exam. (past regret)
If only I ___ (not/say) that to her. (past regret)
I wish you ___ (stop) making so much noise. (complaint)
items.explanation: A complaint about someone else's behavior — wish + would.

items.prompt: Which sentence expresses a present wish (not a past regret)?
options: I wish I had learned to swim.
I wish I knew how to swim.
I wish I had known how to swim.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly complains about someone else's habit?
options: I wish he would stop smoking.
items.explanation: "Wish + would" is the standard form for complaining about someone's behavior.

items.incorrect: I wish I have a bigger house.
answer: I wish I had a bigger house.
items.explanation: A present wish needs the past simple.

items.incorrect: If only I studied harder when I was young. (looking back with regret)
answer: If only I had studied harder when I was young.
items.explanation: A past regret needs the past perfect.

summary: Wish/if only + past simple = a present wish (reality is different now).
Wish/if only + past perfect = a past regret.
Wish + would = a complaint about someone else's behavior — not used for yourself.
